t.6.94.1: The king of men beheld that chariot of the king of the rākṣasas, bearing a great banner and resounding loudly, as it came rushing suddenly upon him.
t.6.94.3: Seeing the enemy's chariot rushing toward him like a cloud, its roar like that of a mountain splitting apart when struck by the thunderbolt, Rāma spoke to Mātali, the charioteer of the thousand-eyed Indra.
t.6.94.2: Yoked with black horses and endowed with a fierce splendour, thick with banners like flashes of lightning and displaying weapons like rainbows, it released streams of arrows like a cloud pouring down torrents of rain.
t.6.94.5: Therefore remain vigilant and drive forward to meet the enemy's chariot; I wish to destroy it as the wind scatters a risen cloud.
t.6.94.4: Mātali, look at the enemy's chariot rushing furiously toward us! Since he again sweeps around to the left with tremendous speed, it is clear that he has set his mind on bringing about his own death in battle.
t.6.94.6: Drive the chariot swiftly, steady and free of confusion, with heart and eye undistracted, keeping it governed by the movement of the reins.
t.6.94.7: Indeed, you who are accustomed to Puraṃdara's chariot need no direction. Eager for battle and single-minded, I only remind you; I do not instruct you.
t.6.94.8: Pleased by those words of Rāma, Mātali, the best of the charioteers of the gods, urged the chariot onward.
t.6.94.9: Then, circling Rāvaṇa's great chariot so as to keep it on his right, he engulfed Rāvaṇa in the dust thrown up by his wheels.
t.6.94.10: Then the enraged Daśagrīva, his eyes red as copper and opened wide, assailed with his arrows Rāma, who stood facing his chariot.
t.6.94.11: Rāma, enraged by the assault and overstepping his composure through wrath, seized in battle the Aindra bow of tremendous force; and he of exceedingly great splendour took up arrows whose radiance equalled the rays of the sun.
t.6.94.12: Then a great battle began between the two, each eager to slay the other and facing one another like two proud lions.
t.6.94.13: Then the gods together with the Gandharvas, the Siddhas and the supreme sages, longing for the destruction of Rāvaṇa, came together to witness the single combat of chariot against chariot.
t.6.94.14: Then terrible, hair-raising portents arose, foretelling the destruction of Rāvaṇa and the victory of Rāghava.
t.6.94.15: The god of rain showered blood upon Rāvaṇa's chariot, and fierce whirling winds began to circle from right to left.
t.6.94.16: And a great flock of vultures, wheeling in the sky, raced along after him wherever his chariot went.
t.6.94.17: And Laṅkā, enveloped by a twilight glow resembling the japā flower, appeared like a land set ablaze even in the daytime.
t.6.94.18: Then great meteors, hostile and loud-roaring, streaked forth with thunderclaps, filling Rāvaṇa's rākṣasas with dismay.
t.6.94.19: And wherever Rāvaṇa was, there the earth shook, and the arms of the rākṣasas as they struck were as if seized and held fast.
t.6.94.20: The rays of the sun that had fallen upon Rāvaṇa's body appeared coppery, yellow, pale and white, like the colored minerals on a mountain.
t.6.94.21: Followed by vultures, she-jackals spewing fire from their mouths howled loudly as they gazed upon his wrathful and inauspicious face.
t.6.94.22: In the battle the wind blew contrary, scattering up the dust and blinding the eyes of that king of the Rākṣasas.
t.6.94.23: Terrible thunderbolts of Indra, with unbearable roars, fell on all sides upon his army, even without the rumbling of clouds.
t.6.94.24: All the directions and the intermediate quarters were shrouded in darkness, and because of a great shower of dust the sky became hard to see.
t.6.94.25: Making a terrible clamour, mynah birds in their hundreds, fierce and harsh-voiced, swooped down there upon his chariot.
t.6.94.26: His horses ceaselessly shed sparks from their hindquarters and tears from their eyes, pouring forth fire and water alike.
t.6.94.27: Many dreadful portents of this kind, bringing fear, arose, foreboding the destruction of Rāvaṇa.
t.6.94.28: For Rāma too there appeared omens on every side, gentle and auspicious, proclaiming victory.
t.6.94.29: Then Rāghava, skilled in reading omens, beholding the omens that appeared concerning himself in the battle, attained joy and supreme contentment, and displayed still greater valour in the fight.
